criteria.declared: A packet names the declared items it claims, explicitly. It is not inferred from the packet's prose: packets are reused and their outcome text goes stale, which mis-mapped two reviews the first time this was measured.
Each declared criterion of each claimed item is scored against the packet's acceptance criteria, and a criterion no acceptance criterion tests refuses to open the review.
The gate is monotonic. It can refuse to open a review and can never approve one, because a score that removes a gate fails open exactly where being wrong matters most.
Opening anyway requires an explicit flag, and the review state records that it was overridden rather than covered.

A scorer that did not run is recorded as not run, never as covered. Not running it authorises nothing, so it must not block every review on a paid third-party service; it must also never let a later reader believe coverage was checked when it was not.
The extractor's own coverage is checked by a second independent count, and a partial extraction refuses to score rather than passing over what it did not read.
